key_insight: Auditing ASR systems should be driven by the people and communities affected — not only by technical metrics — so that evaluations capture real-world harms, contextual use cases, and intersectional disparities.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between standard, opaque ASR evaluations (e.g., aggregate WER) and the lived harms experienced by diverse users; reduces missed biases, poor real-world performance, and lack of accountability in deployed speech systems.
method: Stakeholder-centered audit design: identify affected groups (speakers, clinicians, callers, developers) and co-design evaluation goals and metrics with them.
Disaggregated, context-aware measurement: evaluate ASR across demographic intersections, dialects, acoustic contexts, and downstream tasks rather than relying on single aggregate scores.

Transparent, iterative process and reporting: document datasets, protocols, limitations and remediation steps; embed audits into development lifecycles for continuous monitoring and stakeholder feedback.
impact: Helps practitioners build, evaluate, and deploy ASR systems that are safer, fairer, and more accountable by aligning technical evaluation with stakeholder priorities; supports regulatory compliance and trust with end users.
visual_elements: Flowchart of a stakeholder-driven audit cycle: stakeholder mapping → co-designed metrics → disaggregated testing → remediation → public reporting

paper_title: The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition
paper_authors: Mona Sloane, Hilke Schellmann, Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Allison Koenecke
